title: Refresh docs/firestore-collection-layout.md to match the current firestore.rules and firestore.indexes.json

evidence.quote: The Firestore SDK converts ISO-8601 strings into Timestamp objects on write, so this format is safe to use in push documents.
in Firestore Security Rules a `string <= timestamp` comparison is `false`, which would deny EVERY completion create.

why: The doc's header claims 'Status: current -- reconciled ... 2026-05-18 (Wave 2)', but firestore.rules has since gone through W3.32-W3.43 and the V2-R3 tutor-access rework, none of which are reflected: it says the indexes file declares zero composite indexes when it declares six; it describes a 3-part rules structure (default-deny, top-level compat blocks, live nested) when the compat blocks (accounts/completion_events/track_configs/etc.) no longer exist in the file at all; it documents a `streak` snapshot singleton that was replaced by `streak_events` (W3.37); it lists notification_settings/gamification_settings/ui_preferences as three separate collections when they were unified into `preferences/{scope}` (W3.33); and it never mentions tutor_grants/tutor_active_access/audit_log -- the highest-risk, cross-user part of the whole schema -- at all. A developer or AI agent trusting this 'canonical' doc would reason from a materially wrong model of the app's Firestore security surface.
recommendation: Regenerate the collection tables and 'Security rules' section from the current firestore.rules/firestore.indexes.json, and add the tutor_grants/tutor_active_access/audit_log subsystem.
acceptance_criteria: The doc's index-count claim, collection tables, and rules-structure description all match a fresh read of firestore.rules/firestore.indexes.json.
The doc documents tutor_grants, tutor_active_access, and audit_log.
mergedFrom: Correct FirestoreCodec.encodeDateTime's false claim that the Firestore SDK auto-converts ISO-8601 strings to Timestamp
